- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast increase to +2–4% above peak.
- If supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model underestimates price volatility; add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to mean.
- If sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–2% downward buffer.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count (≥18 events), model tends to lag true price movements; shift forecast 1–3 days ahead by +0.5–1.5% per event.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment after 3 consecutive bullish days.
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (e.g., 3+ per 30d), model overestimates price stability; reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per event.
